title: Jane Austen's birth chart
metaDescription: Jane Austen's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.5° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Saturn sit 0.4° from an exact square — near enough that the tradition reads drive and structure as a single working part. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 24.5° Sagittarius. That falls in the third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 5.5° Sagittarius; Venus stands at 9.1° Scorpio; Mars stands at 19.2° Capricorn. The tradition reads a mind that decides at speaking speed from Mercury, taste tuned to mood and undertow from Venus, drive that grinds rather than flares from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars to Saturn is the closest call of the day, a square within 0.4°. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, the Sun square Neptune at 0.4°, and Neptune trine Pluto at 0.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, five sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 5.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Scorpio at 9.1° is in detriment; Mars in Capricorn at 19.2° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Gemini at 15.6° is in detriment; Saturn in Libra at 19.6° is in exaltation. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 4, earth 3, fire 2, water 1 across the elements, and mutable 5, cardinal 4, fixed 1 across the modalities. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.2° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 8.9°.
